Verified IDs, exact target_refs, question_refs=[], required tags, status=draft, HTTPS links and counts 2–5, and body lengths 166/159/156/153 words. All fields match; all four bodies lack the required useful headings.

Actually opened all six unique cited URLs on 2026-10-09, including Spitzer. IAU confirms Canes Venatici/CVn, Monoceros/Mon, Serpens/Ser, Capricornus/Cap. URLs and claim-level support appear in source_visits.

NASA supports M51 in Canes Venatici, spiral/star-forming structure, pink star-forming regions and blue clusters; its arms compress hydrogen. NASA describes a close encounter with NGC 5195 as the likely contributor to arm prominence and triggered star formation, explicitly attributing the explanation to some astronomers. Spitzer identifies the interacting pair as NGC 5194/5195 in Canes Venatici. The draft preserves the hypothesis qualification.

NASA supports the Rosette as a Monoceros star-forming region at one end of a giant molecular cloud, about 5,000 ly away and 100 ly across; it says young-star radiation makes gas glow. The same page supports DSS for the background, Hubble for the inset, dark hydrogen/dust silhouettes and colors associated with hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen. No factual correction required.

NASA supports M16 in Serpens; Pillars of Creation; IC 4703 as emission nebula and NGC 6611 as open cluster; infrared revealing young stars and background stars hidden at visible wavelengths. NASA says UV bathes the pillars while stellar winds slowly erode gas/dust. Draft's UV-evaporation causal wording overstates the cited source and should be corrected.

NASA supports M30 in Capricornus, globular-cluster type and about 28,000 ly; NASA identifies two blue-straggler pathways: near head-on stellar collisions and binary hydrogen transfer. The draft correctly treats the youthful appearance as not proof of recent birth.
